questions.question: What is the sum of all two-digit numbers divisible by both 3 and 5?
questions.explanation: LCM of (3 and 5) = 15. Two-digit multiples of 15: 15 to 90 (AP with a = 15, d = 15, n = 6). Sum = (n/2)(a + l) = (6/2)(15 + 90) = 315.

The LCM of two prime numbers x and y (x > y) is 533. The value of 4y - x is:
questions.explanation: LCM of two prime numbers x, y is x × y = 533. 533 = 13 × 41. Since x > y, x = 41, y = 13. Value of 4y - x = 4(13) - 41 = 52 - 41 = 11.

Five bells commence tolling together and toll at intervals of 5, 10, 15, 20 and 25 seconds respectively. In 1 hour 20 minutes, how many times do they toll together?
questions.explanation: LCM(5, 10, 15, 20, 25) = 300 seconds. 1 hour 20 minutes = 80 minutes = 80 × 60 = 4800 seconds. Number of times = (4800 / 300) + 1 = 16 + 1 = 17 times.

questions.question: There is a circular path around a sports field. Rahul takes 15 minutes to drive one round of the field, while Anil takes 18 minutes for the same. Suppose they both start from the same point and at the same time, and go in the same direction. After how many minutes will they meet again at the starting point?
Let x = 224 and, y = 322. If the highest common factor of 23x and a × y is divisible by x and y, then what can be the possible value of a ?
questions.explanation: x = 224 = 2^5 × 7. y = 322 = 2 × 7 × 23. 23x = 23 × 2^5 × 7. a × y = a × 2 × 7 × 23. For HCF to be divisible by x (2^5 × 7) and y (2 × 7 × 23), a must contribute factor 2^4 = 16.

120 apples, 240 oranges and 150 pears are packed in cartons in such a way that each carton has the same number of fruits, each carton contains only one type of fruit and fruit is left unpacked. What is the smallest possible number of cartons needed for the purpose ?

The traffic lights at 3 different road crossings change after every 48 sec, 72 sec and 108 sec, respectively. If they all change simentionusly at 8 : 20 a.m., then at what will they next change again simultaneously?
questions.explanation: LCM(48, 72, 108) = 432 seconds = 7 minutes 12 seconds. Time = 8:20 a.m. + 7 min 12 sec = 8:27:12 a.m.

questions.question: A and B are two prime numbers such that A > B and their LCM is 209. The value of A² - B is ?
questions.explanation: A × B = 209. Primes whose product is 209 are 19 and 11. Since A > B, A = 19, B = 11. A² - B = 19² - 11 = 361 - 11 = 350.

questions.question: 13, a, b, c are four distinct numbers and the HCF of each pair of numbers (13, a) : (13, b) : (13, c) is 13, where a, b, c are each less than 60 and a < b < c. What is the value of (a + c)/b ?
questions.explanation: Since HCF(13, a) = HCF(13, b) = HCF(13, c) = 13 with numbers < 60 and a < b < c, the multiples of 13 under 60 are 26, 39, 52. So a = 26, b = 39, c = 52. (a + c)/b = (26 + 52)/39 = 78/39 = 2.

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 1215 and their HCF is 81. If the numbers lie between 500 and 700, then the sum of reciprocals of the numbers is
questions.explanation: Let numbers be 81x and 81y. 81(x + y) = 1215 => x + y = 15. Since numbers lie between 500 and 700, x = 8 and y = 7 (81×8=648, 81×7=567). Sum of reciprocals = 1/648 + 1/567 = (7 + 8)/(81 × 56) = 15 / (81 × 56) = 5 / 1512.

questions.question: If r is the remainder when each of 6454, 7306 and 8797 is divided by the greatest number d (d > 1), then (d - r) is:
In finding the HCF of two numbers by division method, the quotients are 1, 8 and 2 respectively, and the last divisor is 105, what is the sum of the numbers ?
questions.explanation: Reverse division: Last divisor = 105, quotient = 2 => number = 105 × 2 = 210. Next number = 210 × 8 + 105 = 1785. Next number = 1785 × 1 + 210 = 1995. The two numbers are 1785 and 1995. Sum = 1785 + 1995 = 3780.

questions.question: When the smallest number x is divided by 5, 6, 8, 9 and 12, it gives remainder 1 in each case. But x is divisible by 13. What will be the remainder when x will be divided by 31?
questions.explanation: LCM(5, 6, 8, 9, 12) = 360. Number x = 360k + 1. For x to be divisible by 13: 360k + 1 = 13(27k) + (9k + 1). For k = 10, 9(10) + 1 = 91 (divisible by 13). x = 360(10) + 1 = 3601. When 3601 is divided by 31: 3601 = 31 × 116 + 5 => Remainder = 5.

questions.question: The Highest Common Factor and Lowest Common Multiple of two numbers p and q are A and B respectively. If A + B = p + q, then the value of A³ + B³ is :
questions.explanation: HCF = A, LCM = B. A × B = pq. Given A + B = p + q. A³ + B³ = (A + B)³ - 3AB(A + B) = (p + q)³ - 3pq(p + q) = p³ + q³.

questions.question: What is the largest number that divides 460, 491 and 553 and leaves the remainder 26 in each case ?
A is the smallest three-digit number which when divided by 3, 4 and 5 gives remainder 1, 2 and 3 respectively. What is the sum of the digits of A ?
questions.explanation: 3 - 1 = 2, 4 - 2 = 2, 5 - 3 = 2. LCM(3, 4, 5) = 60. Number form = 60k - 2. For smallest 3-digit number, k = 2: A = 60(2) - 2 = 118. Sum of digits = 1 + 1 + 8 = 10.

questions.question: The product of two numbers is 6760 and their HCF is 13. How many such pairs of numbers can be formed?
questions.explanation: Let numbers be 13x and 13y. 13x × 13y = 6760 => 169xy = 6760 => xy = 40. Co-prime pairs (x, y) = (1, 40) and (5, 8). There are 2 such pairs.

questions.question: How many numbers between 400 and 700 are divisible by 5, 6 and 7 ?
questions.explanation: LCM(5, 6, 7) = 210. Multiples of 210 between 400 and 700 are 420 and 630. There are 2 numbers.

When 12, 16, 18, 20 and 25 divide the least number x, the remainder in each case is 4 but x is divisible by 7. What is the digit at the thousands’ place in x ?
questions.explanation: LCM(12, 16, 18, 20, 25) = 3600. x = 3600k + 4. For x to be divisible by 7: 3600k + 4 = 7(514k) + (2k + 4). For k = 5, 2(5) + 4 = 14 (divisible by 7). x = 3600(5) + 4 = 18004. Digit at thousands' place is 8.

questions.question: What is the least square number that is divisible by 6, 9, and 15?
questions.explanation: LCM(6, 9, 15) = 90 = 2 × 3² × 5. To make it a square, multiply by 2 × 5 = 10 => 90 × 10 = 900.

questions.question: What is the least square number that is exactly divisible by 3, 5, 12, and 15?
questions.explanation: LCM(3, 5, 12, 15) = 60 = 2² × 3 × 5. To make it a square, multiply by 3 × 5 = 15 => 60 × 60 = 3600.

Three red lights on the same road start blinking at the same time and blink repeatedly after every 4, 6 and 8 minutes, respectively. How many times will they blink together in an interval of 3 hours, excluding blinking together at the starting moment ?
questions.explanation: LCM(4, 6, 8) = 24 minutes. 3 hours = 180 minutes. Times blinking together = 180 / 24 = 7.5 => 7 times.

questions.question: As part of the partial work from home process, Amita went to office every 2nd day, Amrita went to office every 3rd day, and Tosita went to office every 6th day, respectively. All three went to office on 31 October 2021. On how many days did all three attend office on the same date during the remaining two months of the year ?
questions.explanation: LCM(2, 3, 6) = 6 days. Remaining two months (Nov + Dec) = 30 + 31 = 61 days. Number of times = 61 / 6 = 10 times.

questions.question: x, y and z are divisible by 2, 3 and 4, respectively. What is the highest common factor (HCF) of 6x, 4y and 3z ?
questions.explanation: x = 2k => 6x = 12k. y = 3m => 4y = 12m. z = 4n => 3z = 12n. Each is a multiple of 12. HCF is at least 12.

Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 4. The product of their HCF and LCM is 2700. The sum of the numbers is:
questions.explanation: Let numbers be 3x and 4x. HCF × LCM = Product = 12x² = 2700 => x² = 225 => x = 15. Sum = 3(15) + 4(15) = 105.

The least number which should be added to 1351 so that the sum is exactly divisible by 2, 4, 6 and 8 is:
questions.explanation: LCM(2, 4, 6, 8) = 24. 1351 / 24 gives remainder 7. Number to add = 24 - 7 = 17.

questions.question: Let the HCF of m and n be 'a' and let n = ab, LCM of m and n is given by:
questions.explanation: HCF(m, n) = a, n = ab. LCM × HCF = m × n => LCM × a = m × (ab) => LCM = mb.

questions.question: The LCM and HCF of two numbers are 1105 and 5. If the LCM is 17 times the first number, then find the two numbers.
questions.explanation: LCM = 1105, HCF = 5. LCM = 17 × first number => first number = 1105 / 17 = 65. Second number = (1105 × 5) / 65 = 85. Numbers are 65 and 85.

The LCM of two numbers is five times their HCF. If the product of the two numbers is 20480, then find their HCF and LCM, respectively.
questions.explanation: LCM = 5 × HCF. Product = HCF × LCM = 5 × HCF² = 20480 => HCF² = 4096 => HCF = 64. LCM = 5 × 64 = 320.

questions.question: If the sum of two numbers is 60 and their HCF and LCM are 5 and 60, respectively, then the sum of the reciprocals of the numbers will be:
questions.explanation: a + b = 60, ab = HCF × LCM = 5 × 60 = 300. Sum of reciprocals = (a + b)/ab = 60/300 = 1/5.

questions.explanation: HCF must divide LCM. 74 is not divisible by 12, so 74 can never be the LCM.

questions.question: The product of two numbers is 4107. If the HCF of these numbers is 37, then the greater number is:
questions.explanation: Product = 4107, HCF = 37. Product of co-prime ratios xy = 4107 / (37²) = 3. Pairs = (1, 3). Greater number = 37 × 3 = 111.

Find the smallest three digit number which when added to 5 is exactly divisible by 12, 14 and 18.
questions.explanation: LCM(12, 14, 18) = 252. Smallest 3-digit number added to 5 = 252 => Number = 252 - 5 = 247.

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers is 3 : 4. If the sum of these two numbers is 70, then what is their LCM ?
questions.explanation: Numbers = 3x, 4x. 3x + 4x = 70 => 7x = 70 => x = 10. Numbers are 30 and 40. LCM(30, 40) = 120.

questions.question: Find the least number divisible by 2, 3, 5, 6, 9 and 18, which is a perfect square.
questions.explanation: LCM(2, 3, 5, 6, 9, 18) = 90 = 2 × 3² × 5. To make it a square, multiply by 2 × 5 = 10 => 90 × 10 = 900.

The HCF of two numbers is one-twentieth of their LCM. If one of the numbers is 96 and the difference of the LCM and the HCF is 456, then what is the other number ?
questions.explanation: Let LCM = 20u, HCF = 1u. Difference = 19u = 456 => u = 24. LCM = 480, HCF = 24. Product = 480 × 24 = 96 × other => other = 120.

questions.question: What is the HCF of two prime numbers X and Y ?
questions.explanation: The HCF of any two distinct prime numbers is always 1.

questions.question: What is that least number that should be added to 478 so that the number obtained becomes exactly divisible by 5, 6 and 12 ?
questions.explanation: LCM(5, 6, 12) = 60. 478 / 60 gives remainder 58. Number to add = 60 - 58 = 2.

questions.question: The product of two co-prime numbers is 483. Find the Least Common Multiple of both numbers.
questions.explanation: For co-prime numbers, HCF = 1. LCM × HCF = Product => LCM = Product = 483.

questions.question: What is the smallest perfect square which is divisible by both 8 and 12 ?
questions.explanation: LCM(8, 12) = 24 = 2³ × 3. To make a square, multiply by 2 × 3 = 6 => 24 × 6 = 144.

questions.question: The product of the two numbers is 1500 and their HCF is 10. The number of such possible pairs is/are:
questions.explanation: Let numbers be 10x and 10y. 10x × 10y = 1500 => xy = 15. Co-prime pairs: (1, 15) and (3, 5). Total 2 pairs.

questions.question: If the highest common factor (HCF) of x and y is 15, then the HCF of 36x² - 81y² and 81x² - 9y² is divisible by
questions.explanation: Let x = 15a, y = 15b. 36x² - 81y² = 9(2x - 3y)(2x + 3y) = 9 × 15 × (factor). 81x² - 9y² = 9(3x - y)(3x + y) = 9 × 15 × (factor). HCF has factor 9 × 15 = 135.
